name: Frequency Counting (Hash Map)
description: Counts occurrences of elements using an object or Map as a hash table. The most common hash map pattern in interviews, used for finding duplicates, majority elements, anagram grouping, and relative sort.

examples.title: Example 1: Find Majority Element (> n/2 times)
examples.explanation: Two-pass: first counts frequencies, second finds majority. Boyer-Moore variant uses O(1) space. Time O(n), Space O(n) or O(1).

examples.title: Example 2: Valid Anagram Check
examples.explanation: Count chars in s, decrement with t. If any count goes negative or key missing, not an anagram. Time O(n), Space O(1) assuming 26 lowercase chars (or O(k) where k=char set size).

name: Caching & Memoization
description: Stores previously computed results to avoid redundant calculations. Used for optimizing recursive algorithms (DP), expensive function calls, and reducing time complexity from exponential to polynomial.

examples.title: Example 1: Fibonacci with Memoization
examples.explanation: Memoization caches recursive calls, turning O(2^n) into O(n). Iterative DP builds bottom-up. Space-optimized keeps only last two values. Time O(n), Space O(n) or O(1).

examples.title: Example 2: LRU Cache using Map
examples.explanation: JavaScript Map maintains insertion order. get() refreshes position by delete+reinsert. put() evicts oldest entry (first key) when full. All operations O(1) average. Time O(1), Space O(capacity).

name: Grouping & Multi-set Indexing
description: Groups elements by a key or property. Common for grouping anagrams, people by city, transactions by date, or building lookups from arrays. Can use object or Map depending on key type.

examples.title: Example 1: Group Anagrams
examples.explanation: Sort each word to get canonical form as key. Optimized version counts chars (O(n) instead of O(n log n)) and joins with delimiter to avoid ambiguity. Time O(n * k log k) or O(n*k), Space O(n*k).

examples.title: Example 2: Index Array by Value (Two Sum pré-compute)
examples.explanation: Store each number's index as we scan. For current num, check if complement exists. If found, return both indices. Map preferred over object for cleaner semantics and guaranteed O(1) hashing. Time O(n), Space O(n).

name: Set for Uniqueness & Fast Lookup
description: JavaScript Set provides O(1) average insert, delete, and lookup. Used for deduplication, intersection/union operations, cycle detection, and checking membership without duplicates.

examples.title: Example 1: Remove Duplicates & Check Distinct
examples.explanation: Set.has() is O(1) average. Spread operator + Set removes duplicates. Intersection iterates smaller array into Set, then checks against larger. Time O(n+m), Space O(min(n,m)).

examples.title: Example 2: Happy Number (Cycle Detection with Set)
examples.explanation: Set detects cycles by remembering seen states. If we repeat a number, we're in a loop. Floyd's algorithm uses two pointers (slow/fast) to detect cycle with O(1) space. Time O(log n) per iteration, Space O(log n) or O(1).
